dict_examples.en: What do you usually do on weekends? What's your hobby?
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.en: What's your boyfriend's hobby? — Gaming.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

explain_en: A common question when getting to know someone. Answer with ‘제 취미는 N이에요’ or ‘저는 N을/를 좋아해요’. To elders, ‘취미가 어떻게 되세요?’ is more polite.

examples.en: My husband is a good cook.
My younger sibling is a good swimmer.

explain: ‘잘하다’는 한 단어라서 붙여 쓰고, 앞에 ‘을/를’을 써요: 요리를 잘해요. 반대는 ‘못해요’예요. 칭찬을 들으면 한국 사람들은 겸손하게 ‘아니에요, 잘 못해요’라고 많이 대답해요.

dict_examples.en: My friend speaks Korean well.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.ko: 춤을 정말 잘해요! — 아니에요, 잘 못해요.
dict_examples.en: You're a really good dancer! — Oh no, I'm not that good.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.en: My older brother is good at every sport.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

explain_en: ‘잘하다’ is one word, written without a space, and takes ‘을/를’: 요리를 잘해요. The opposite is ‘못해요’. When complimented, Koreans often answer modestly: ‘아니에요, 잘 못해요’ (Oh no, I'm not good at it).

examples.en: I make rice cakes with my mother.
I make a cake for birthdays.

explain: ‘만들다’는 ㄹ 받침 동사라서 ‘만드세요’, ‘만드는’처럼 ㄹ이 빠질 때가 있어요. 음식에도 ‘김밥을 만들어요’처럼 많이 쓰고, 불을 쓰는 요리는 ‘요리해요’라고도 해요.

dict_examples.en: I make gimbap with my friend on weekends.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.en: It's snowing. The children are making a snowman.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.en: Our company makes mobile apps.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

explain_en: 만들다 is an ㄹ-stem verb, so the ㄹ drops in forms like 만드세요 and 만드는. It is used for food too ('김밥을 만들어요'), and cooking with heat can also be called 요리해요.

examples.en: I'm buying a birthday present for my friend.
I buy clothes at the department store.

explain: 받침이 있으면 ‘을’, 없으면 ‘를’을 써요: ‘옷을’, ‘커피를’. 사는 곳은 ‘에서’로 말해요: ‘마트에서 우유를 사요’. 반대말은 ‘팔아요’예요.

dict_examples.en: I buy apples and milk at the supermarket.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.ko: 매일 아침 회사 앞에서 커피를 사요.
dict_examples.en: Every morning I buy coffee in front of my office.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.en: What are you buying? — I'm buying sneakers.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

explain_en: Use 을 after a consonant and 를 after a vowel: 옷을, 커피를. Mark the place where you buy with 에서: '마트에서 우유를 사요.' The opposite is 팔아요 (to sell).

examples.en: I read the newspaper in the morning.
I watch dramas in the evening.

explain: ‘보다’는 눈으로 보는 것 말고도 여러 곳에 써요: 영화를 봐요, 시험을 봐요(take a test), 장을 봐요(grocery shopping). 신문이나 책은 ‘읽어요’도 쓰지만, 가볍게 훑어볼 때는 ‘봐요’라고 해요.

dict_examples.en: I watch videos on my phone during breaks.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.en: I'm taking a Korean test tomorrow.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.en: I do the grocery shopping at the supermarket in the evening.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

explain_en: ‘보다’ is used for more than seeing: 영화를 봐요 (watch a movie), 시험을 봐요 (take a test), 장을 봐요 (do the grocery shopping). For newspapers and books you can say ‘읽어요’, but ‘봐요’ is used for a quick look.

examples.en: I wear socks at home.
I'm wearing sneakers today.

explain: 신발, 양말, 스타킹처럼 발에 하는 것은 ‘신어요’예요. 옷은 ‘입어요’, 모자와 안경은 ‘써요’, 시계는 ‘차요’로 달라요. 반대는 ‘신발을 벗어요’예요.

dict_examples.en: It's raining. I'm putting on rain boots.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.en: When I go inside the house, I put on slippers.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.en: The child puts on shoes by herself.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

explain_en: Use 신어요 for things on your feet: shoes, socks, stockings. Clothes take 입어요, hats and glasses take 써요, and watches take 차요. The opposite is '신발을 벗어요' (take off shoes).
